cloud.failure_mode: A saved stock key keeps local control working. An owner-selected Config.Key installation needs its compatible owner broker only for MQTT, not for LAN /config. Unknown keys and unsupported setup flows cannot be bypassed.
cloud.vendor_service: Meross cloud supplies stock account onboarding and MQTT remote access; established LAN messages do not traverse it.

garage_close.advanced_reason: The door can close onto a person, animal or vehicle without line of sight. Keep the opening clear and watched until physically closed; the contact sensor is not an interlock.
garage_close.body_transform: Signed envelope; Encrypt.Suite AES-256-CBC when advertised.
garage_close.description: Attended SET GarageDoor.State channel 0 open=0 with the bound UUID; never an unattended-close automation.

garage_open.advanced_reason: The door may open immediately and remain unattended. Confirm identity, location and obstructions; monitor actual contact state to completion.
garage_open.body_transform: Signed envelope; Encrypt.Suite AES-256-CBC when advertised.
garage_open.description: Attended SET GarageDoor.State channel 0 open=1 with the bound UUID.

get_garage_state.body_transform: Signed envelope; Encrypt.Suite AES-256-CBC when advertised.
get_garage_state.description: GET GarageDoor.State channel 0; use actual contact/digest state rather than assuming the last command succeeded.

returns.description: 0 closed / 1 open when reported; not a safety verdict.
returns.name: state.open

get_system_all.body_transform: Wrap in the signed Meross envelope; System.All is exempt from Encrypt.Suite.
get_system_all.description: Read identity, abilities and current relay/garage digest in the always-cleartext System.All namespace.

returns.description: Per-channel contact state when present; not a safety interlock.
returns.name: all.digest.garageDoor

owner_config_key.advanced_reason: Rebinds account and MQTT configuration on the physical appliance and invalidates clients using the old key. Use only on the supported legacy setup AP after recording recovery details.
owner_config_key.body_transform: Signed legacy setup-AP envelope; do not send on an unknown Encrypt.Suite/ECDHE setup flow.
owner_config_key.description: Legacy setup-AP-only Config.Key provisioning with deliberately selected account/broker material.

account_key.description: Owner-selected replacement shared key, not recovered stock material.

mqtt_host.description: Owner-controlled broker hostname compatible with this firmware's transport/TLS expectations.

togglex_off.advanced_reason: Attended mains relay write: removing power may interrupt equipment or its shutdown sequence. Confirm the load and read back System.All.
togglex_off.body_transform: Signed envelope; Encrypt.Suite AES-256-CBC when advertised.
togglex_off.description: SET ToggleX channel 0 onoff=0 through the signed/encrypted Meross transform.

togglex_on.advanced_reason: Attended mains relay write: onoff=1 can energize equipment. Confirm the channel and attached load, then read back System.All.
togglex_on.body_transform: Signed envelope; Encrypt.Suite AES-256-CBC when advertised.
togglex_on.description: SET ToggleX channel 0 onoff=1 through the signed/encrypted Meross transform.

methods.notes: Bind client UDP 9989 before sending to broadcast 9988. The vector uses userid 123456: id = MD5(userid), devName = *. Send once per second for five sends and read replies (up to 300 bytes in the reviewed app) for five seconds. Match UUID/MAC to the intended bound device.

response_match.description: Bound-device replies carry a Meross UUID; match it to the intended account/device before control.

identification.notes: A valid UDP-9988 JSON reply with uuid/mac/deviceType is the strong signal. Never infer Meross from HTTP/80 or a MAC prefix.

device.name: Meross Wi-Fi Plugs, Switches and MSG100 Garage Opener
device.notes:
SCOPE: Meross Wi-Fi plugs/switches using Appliance.Control.ToggleX and the MSG100 garage opener using Appliance.GarageDoor.State. The shared signed envelope, UDP discovery and optional Encrypt.Suite body protection apply to both. Bulbs, thermostats, hubs, BLE-only sensors, Matter and roller shutters are outside this version.
Integration is identify_only because no dedicated Meross discovery, signed envelope, Encrypt.Suite and bound-identity handler exists here. Documentary commands require that transform and are not plain JSON posts for a generic consumer. The protocol itself is native LAN once the matching account key is known; identify_only is not a claim that local control is impossible.

openness.notes: The local JSON protocol is community-documented, not an official open API. meross_lan and MerossIot are maintained implementation references.

enter_pairing_mode.notes: Changing provisioning credentials requires the exact model's setup AP; steady-state signed LAN control does not require a button press.

exclusivity.recovery: Close competing writers and rediscover by UUID/MAC. A wrong account key must fail visibly rather than falling back to another identity or cloud relay.

pairing.notes: Local authorization is possession of shared account material plus the bound UUID/MAC. There is no universal default key and no supported bypass for an Encrypt.Suite setup flow whose ECDHE reply is not established.

pin.notes: The secret is the stock account key or a key deliberately selected during supported legacy Config.Key provisioning, not a device-label PIN.

unpair.clears: On a supported legacy setup AP, deliberately replacing Config.Key replaces the shared account/broker credential used by every client; it does not extract or selectively revoke the old stock key.
unpair.notes: Update every owner client after replacement. No per-client cryptographic identity is created.

safety_advisory.detail: MSG100 relay output can start a door moving and can close onto a person, animal, vehicle or obstruction. Require an attended action and a clear opening, follow the opener's own safety instructions, and verify the physical door and photo-eye/obstruction systems. Never treat GarageDoor.State.open as proof that unattended closing is safe. This project's integration is experimental and unaffiliated with Meross.
safety_advisory.summary: A garage-door command can move the door without line of sight; the wired contact sensor is not a safety interlock.

issued_to_client: Stock Meross account user ID/key, or owner-selected replacement user ID/key
Bound UUID and hardware MAC used to derive Encrypt.Suite key
credentials.notes: Legacy Config.Wifi only Base64-encodes credentials; Config.WifiX uses the documented device-derived AES-256-CBC transform on capable firmware. Signed MD5 headers and fixed-IV CBC do not provide modern replay/integrity protection. Keep account keys out of logs and use a trusted segmented LAN.
stored_on_device: Account user ID/key and MQTT broker configuration

factory_reset.description: The MSS110 and MSG100 manuals are linked below, but this spec does not generalize an unreviewed button hold to both families.
factory_reset.effect: A single cross-family reset procedure and the survival of Config.Key, Wi-Fi, relay schedules and garage pairing were not established. Do not substitute a short relay press, RF pairing or MQTT reconfiguration for a factory reset; consult the exact MSS/MSG model guide before clearing it.

methods.description: For a model/firmware known to accept the legacy plaintext setup-AP flow, join the device AP, read System.All/Ability, choose new account material and an owner-controlled MQTT broker, then write Config.Key before Wi-Fi provisioning. Stop and use another supported route if the device requires Encrypt.Suite/ECDHE; that setup exchange is unresolved.
methods.name: Supported legacy AP with owner-selected Config.Key

steps.action: Join the exact model's setup AP after using its manual's setup procedure.
GET Appliance.System.All and Appliance.System.Ability in cleartext and record uuid, hardware MAC and supported namespaces.
steps.expect: Identity is bound to the physical unit; if Encrypt.Suite is required for setup, stop rather than treating legacy Config.Key as universal.

steps.action: Choose a new user ID/key and compatible owner-controlled broker; send Appliance.Config.Key with primary and secondary gateway set to that broker.
steps.expect: The selected key, not a recovered Meross key, will authenticate later LAN signatures and bound-device encryption.

steps.action: Provision Wi-Fi with the model-appropriate Config.Wifi or Config.WifiX shape, then rediscover by UUID/MAC on the LAN.
steps.expect: The appliance joins the chosen network and answers signed local requests.

cloud.local_alternative: Established LAN control uses the saved key locally. Supported legacy AP owners may instead choose new Config.Key material; neither path extracts the other path's key.

methods.description: Provision in the official app, then retain the account key/user ID for subsequent signed LAN requests; no cloud round trip is needed for established local control.

account_key.notes: The existing stock Meross account key, or the different key deliberately selected during supported legacy Config.Key provisioning.

device_uuid.notes: The bound appliance UUID read from UDP discovery or Appliance.System.All and matched to that account key.

methods.name: Official Meross app and existing account key

steps.action: Add the exact model in the Meross app and bind it to the owner's account on a 2.4 GHz network.
steps.expect: The appliance is provisioned and appears in UDP discovery.

steps.action: Store the account user ID/key securely and bind discovered UUID/MAC to that account before signing or deriving Encrypt.Suite keys.
steps.expect: GET/SET signatures verify locally without contacting Meross cloud.

setup.notes: Two different credential paths exist. Stock setup binds the appliance to a Meross account and the owner retains that account key. On supported legacy setup-AP firmware, an owner can instead choose a new user ID/key and MQTT broker through Config.Key. The latter does not reveal an existing stock key and is not universal recovery, especially where setup requires Encrypt.ECDHE.

rejoin.notes: Re-enter the exact model's setup/AP flow to replace Wi-Fi. A setup or pairing mode is not automatically a full factory reset. Config.Key chooses account/broker material, not the Wi-Fi SSID; Config.Wifi/WifiX is a separate step.

steps.action: Use the exact model guide to enter setup mode, preserving the old LAN configuration until the new credentials are ready where possible.
Reprovision Wi-Fi and either retain verified stock account material or deliberately choose new Config.Key material on a supported legacy AP.
steps.expect: Rediscovery resolves the same UUID/MAC; if the key changed, all clients must be updated.

testing.notes: No appliance, garage door, setup AP, UDP discovery or HTTP request was run. Facts are reported from Meross 3.41.1 static analysis, MerossIot, meross_lan and arandall/meross. All account IDs, UUIDs, MACs, keys and vectors are synthetic; no garage or mains relay was actuated.

http_endpoints.description: Cleartext header/payload envelope, or raw Base64 Encrypt.Suite body for non-exempt namespaces. Always target the discovered UUID/MAC.
http_endpoints.name: Signed Meross JSON message

covers: ToggleX plugs/switches and MSG100 garage state/control
Stock account-key local control or deliberately re-provisioned owner-selected credentials
not_covered: Existing stock-key recovery or universal legacy/ECDHE setup
BLE-only devices, lights, hubs, thermostats, roller shutters and Matter
Unattended garage closing, generic safe relay automation or official cloud remote access
local_access.summary: Bound Meross appliances accept signed JSON on LAN HTTP, with optional Encrypt.Suite body encryption; supported legacy AP provisioning can use owner-selected Config.Key material.

config_key.boundary: Owner-selected replacement credentials for supported legacy AP provisioning only. It does not retrieve an existing key, authorize an unknown device, or prove arbitrary broker/TLS settings work on every firmware.

encrypt_suite.cipher: AES-256-CBC, no cipher padding mode; append zero bytes to a 16-byte multiple (always add a full zero block when already aligned), Base64 raw HTTP body. Decrypt and strip trailing zero bytes before JSON parsing. There is no MAC.
encrypt_suite.key_derivation: MD5_hex(uuid[3:22] || account_key[1:9] || mac || account_key[10:28]); use the 32 lowercase hexadecimal ASCII characters as the 32-byte AES-256 key. MAC spelling comes from system.hardware.macAddress and must match exactly.
encrypt_suite.negotiation: If System.Ability contains Appliance.Encrypt.Suite, GET that namespace in cleartext. This version supports only ka=ecdhe256, se=mrskey, ds empty for bound-device control.
encrypt_suite.setup_boundary: Unbound ECDHE on secp256r1 is reported but its reply field/complete setup exchange is unresolved. Bound-device key derivation must not be presented as a setup bypass.

envelope.endpoint: POST http://<address>/config (and http://10.10.10.1/config on setup AP), Connection: close.

acknowledgement: For a normal reply, require method == GETACK when the request was GET, or SETACK when it was SET. Do not accept GET, SET, PUSH, SETACK-for-GET or GETACK-for-SET.

Only after exact ID, namespace and acknowledgement method match, recompute MD5(reply.messageId || account_key || reply.timestamp) and require the reply sign and bound UUID. Only then decode or act on payload.
correlation_first: Require header.messageId to equal the exact outstanding request messageId, not merely a valid MD5 input or a recent response.
Require header.namespace to equal the request's full expected Appliance.* namespace. A valid response for another namespace is not this command's response.
reply_validation.error_path: method == ERROR is a separate device-failure path. After exact ID/namespace correlation, verify its signature and UUID, then surface payload.error.code; never require an ACK method or interpret normal payload as success.
reply_validation.uncorrelated_transport: If a reply lacks the exact ID or arrives while no matching request is outstanding, reject it and serialize the next request with a fresh messageId. Never match replies by arrival order, reuse IDs to make correlation pass, or allow an old reply to complete a later write.
reply_validation.unsolicited_push: PUSH has no outstanding-request correlation. Handle it separately as a state notification after UUID/signature checks, never as the answer that completes an in-flight command.

required_header.from: Full request URL on LAN/AP: http://<address>/config.
required_header.messageId: 32 lowercase hexadecimal characters; the app uses MD5(random 16 [a-z0-9] chars || epoch seconds).
required_header.method: GET or SET for requests; accept GETACK, SETACK, PUSH and ERROR in replies.
required_header.sign: MD5(messageId || account_key || timestamp) as 32 lowercase hexadecimal characters.
required_header.timestamp: Integer epoch seconds, converted to decimal text for signing.
required_header.triggerSrc: AndroidLocal on the reviewed local path; a replacement client may use a stable local identifier only if firmware accepts it.

namespaces.garage_set: SET Appliance.GarageDoor.State with {state:{channel:0,open:0|1,uuid:<device-uuid>}}. open=1 requests open, open=0 requests close; actual contact state must be read back.
namespaces.multiple: Appliance.Control.Multiple can wrap inner {header:{namespace,method},payload} messages; do not nest Multiple or System.All.
namespaces.system_all: GET Appliance.System.All with payload {}; supplies system.firmware.innerIp, system.hardware.macAddress, digest relay/garage state and identity.
namespaces.togglex: GET/SET Appliance.Control.ToggleX with {togglex:{channel:n,onoff:0|1}}. SET changes a real mains relay.

remaining_unknowns: Exact physical factory-reset procedure and state survival for each MSS switch versus MSG100; no universal hold is asserted.
The complete Encrypt.ECDHE unbound setup reply and provisioning exchange; legacy Config.Key is not a substitute.
Which models/firmware enforce timestamp freshness, reply signatures and Encrypt.Suite, and whether UDP id is a strict account filter.
Exact garage digest/open values during travel/fault and all timing behavior; never infer a safe completed movement from a SETACK.
Broker TLS compatibility for owner-selected Config.Key beyond the legacy flow implemented by the pinned pairer.
